pages.text: Archimedes' method: a regular polygon of n sides inside a circle has perimeter n·sin(π/n) times the diameter, short of π by about π³/(6n²). Doubling the sides quarters the error. A straightedge drawn without care adds its own error.
$(thing)Set$(): Polygon sides, Straightedge care.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): A wobbling table: the error varies by ±2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): none beyond the recipe windows.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Fewer sides and less care are faster.
$(thing)Equations$()$(br)Estimate of π: π ≈ n·sin(π/n)$(br)Error: ε = π − n·sin(π/n) + ε_ruler
